items.content:
Winklevoss-backed Cypherpunk buys Zcash dip as mining debut delivers $2.6 million operating profit

Cypherpunk mined $9.9 million worth of ZEC in 44 days and says its mining business is worth more than the value of its holdings.

By Kyle Baird • Edited by Jason Shubnell

Business • November 16, 2026, 1:43PM EST

Cypherpunk’s treasury reached 341,859 ZEC, about 2% of the circulating supply.

Cypherpunk raised $56.5 million through stock sales to fund mining expansion and ZEC purchases.

Cypherpunk Technologies, the Zcash treasury company founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, got back to buying ZEC amid its recent pullback while its mining business recorded its first quarterly profit.

Nasdaq-listed Cypherpunk (CYPH) reported $2.6 million in operating income for the third quarter, following the August launch of its Zcash mining fleet. Net income totaled $306 million, entirely driven by $330.8 million in unrealized gains on its ZEC holdings.

"With the pullback in Zcash, we resumed our open market purchase strategy," CEO Dug Onsi said on Monday's earnings call .

Since quarter-end, Cypherpunk bought another 3,775 ZEC for about $3.5 million at an average price of $920.40. Tacking on October's mining production, its treasury reached more than 341,858 ZEC, which is just over 2% of the entire circulating supply. Cypherpunk aims to hold at least 5% of Zcash's circulating supply, much like the 5% ether supply ownership target set by the Tom Lee-chaired Bitmine .

ZEC was down a further 2% to $887 on Monday, extending its decline over the past month to roughly 22%. In late September, ZEC hit a new all-time high of $1,650.

Cypherpunk mined 8,967 ZEC during the first 44 days of operations, pulling in nearly $10 million in revenue. Hosting costs averaged out to about $104 per token, and all the ZEC it mined were routed into its treasury.

The company also raised $56.5 million through its at-the-market stock offering program in the third quarter. The funds went towards mining equipment and more ZEC purchases.

A portion also covered operating expenses "so we don't have to sell the Zcash that we mined," Onsi said.

CIO Will McEvoy said that mining changes how investors should value the company and that whether its shares trade above or below the value of its crypto holdings — a metric commonly known as mNav — "doesn't make a ton of sense nowadays."

"I think analysts should be sort of looking at the business from a sum-of-the-parts perspective," he said, pointing to its ZEC treasury and mining revenue and earnings.

큐원4 맥스는 2조4000억개 매개변수의 전문가 혼합(MoE) 구조를 갖췄다. 실제 활성화되는 매개변수는 710억개다. 여기에 연속된 토큰의 패턴을 학습하기 위한 3280억개의 별도 N-그램 임베딩 매개변수를 사용한다.

전작인 '큐원3.8 맥스'와 전체 매개변수 규모는 같지만, 활성 매개변수는 950억개에서 710억개로 25% 감소했다. 모델 크기를 늘리지 않고 연산 효율을 높인 것이 특징이다.

새로운 큐원4 아키텍처에는 '게이티드 델타넷(Gated DeltaNet)'과 '큐원 희소 어텐션(Qwen Sparse Attention)' '게이티드 레지듀얼(Gated Residual)' 등이 적용됐다. 긴 문맥을 처리하는 연산량을 줄이고 모델 내부의 정보 전달을 개선해 적은 계산으로 높은 성능을 내도록 설계했다.

실제 외부 평가에서도 성능과 비용 효율성이 개선됐다. 아티피셜 애널리시스의 종합 지능 지수(AAII)에서 43점을 기록해 전작의 34점보다 9점 높아졌다. 작업당 평균 비용도 10.02달러에서 3.27달러로 약 67% 줄었다.

Alibaba has launched Qwen4 Max, gaining 9 points over Qwen3.8 Max on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and landing 3 points behind Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower Cost per Task

Qwen4 Max, using xhigh reasoning effort, scores 43 on the Intelligence Index, 9 points ahead of… pic.twitter.com/dwh719Cq14

— Artificial Analysis (@ArtificialAnlys) November 16, 2026

그러나 중국 최상위 모델과의 경쟁에서는 아직 격차가 있다. 문샷 AI의 '키미 K3.1 프로'는 같은 평가에서 46점을 기록했으며, 작업당 비용은 3.68달러였다. 큐원4 맥스는 비용에서는 앞섰지만 종합 성능은 키미에 미치지 못했다.

세부 평가에서도 강점과 약점이 나타났다. 소프트웨어 개발 평가인 '딥SWE 1.1'에서는 75.7점을 기록해 앤트로픽의 '오퍼스 5.5' 74.2점을 앞섰다. 그러나 터미널 환경에서 소프트웨어 개발 작업을 수행하는 '터미널벤치 4.0'에서는 48.5%로 키미 K3.1의 67.2%에 뒤졌다.

알리바바가 자체 개발한 전문 업무 평가 '워크360(Work360)'에서는 52.69점을 기록해 전작의 47.74점을 넘어섰다. 금융과 법률, 의료, 제조 등 721개 세부 전문 분야를 대상으로 진행한 평가다.

특히 동일한 작업을 처리하는 데 필요한 토큰 사용량이 추론 강도에 따라 24~35% 감소했다. 터미널벤치 4.0에서는 약 48~49% 줄었다. 워크360의 평균 작업 비용도 4.43달러에서 1.67달러로 약 62% 낮아졌다.

Token efficiency and cost: Qwen4-Max outperforms Qwen3.8-Max with fewer tokens. On Work360, token usage drops by approximately 24% (Xhigh) and 35% (High); on Terminal-Bench 4.0, by about 48% and 49%. In our Work360 evaluation, the average cost per task drops from $4.43 to $1.67. pic.twitter.com/FOGlX8ldKM

— Qwen (@Alibaba_Qwen) November 16, 2026

실제 업무를 수행하는 에이전트 평가에서도 개선이 확인됐다. 웹 개발 능력을 평가하는 '코드 아레나'에서 6위에 올랐고, '에이전트 아레나'에서는 전작의 39위에서 14위로 상승했다.

알리바바는 제조와 과학 연구 분야에서의 활용도 강조했다. 자동차 부품 제조 실험에서는 AI가 설계와 가공 과정을 수정해 수작업 프로그래밍 시간을 약 475분에서 24분으로 줄였다고 밝혔다.

반도체 냉각 소재 연구에서는 AI 에이전트를 48시간 동안 실행하며 분자 설계와 합성, 실험, 결과 분석을 반복해 실제 실험으로 검증한 물질 후보를 찾아냈다. 알츠하이머병 관련 연구에서도 새로운 후보 분자 24개를 설계했다고 설명했다.

안전성도 강화했다. 소프트웨어 개발 학습에 보안 검사를 추가하고, 사이버 공격에 활용될 수 있는 학습 데이터를 걸러냈다고 밝혔다. 화학·생물학적 위험 등에 대응하기 위한 안전성 학습도 강화했다는 설명이다.

API 가격은 전작보다 25% 낮아졌다. 큐원4 맥스는 입력 100만 토큰당 1.50달러, 출력 100만 토큰당 4.50달러로, 전작의 2달러와 6달러에서 각각 인하됐다. 반복적으로 사용하는 입력을 캐시로 처리할 때는 100만 토큰당 0.075달러로 기존 0.25달러보다 70% 저렴하다.

큐원4 맥스는 최대 100만 토큰의 컨텍스트를 지원하며 텍스트와 이미지, 동영상을 입력받을 수 있다. 추론 강도도 조절할 수 있다. 기존 프리뷰는 구독형 토큰 플랜에서만 제공됐지만, 정식 모델은 큐원클라우드 에서 종량제 API로 이용할 수 있다. 큐원워크와 큐원 스튜디오, 코더 등 자사 서비스에도 적용됐다.

모델 가중치는 공개하지 않았다. 알리바바는 향후 큐원4 시리즈의 소형 모델들을 오픈웨이트로 공개하겠다고 예고했지만, 구체적인 모델 규모와 일정은 밝히지 않았다.

이번 출시는 알리바바가 AI 모델의 성능뿐 아니라 실제 업무를 처리하는 데 드는 비용을 경쟁력으로 내세우고 있음을 보여준다. 기업들이 AI 에이전트를 반복적으로 활용할수록 토큰 사용량과 작업당 비용이 중요해지는 만큼, 저렴한 고성능 모델을 앞세워 기업용 AI와 클라우드 시장을 공략하려는 전략이다.

items.title: Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: The industry will be ‘fine’
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the special role Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played in the AI boom, but ultimately thinks the industry will be “fine” without him at the helm.
items.content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the AI industry will be “fine” without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the helm, even as he acknowledged the special role Huang has played in the AI boom.

Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement.

Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom.

Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return.

When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the company, Altman said: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.”

He expressed empathy for Huang’s situation, citing his own ousting from OpenAI in 2023 after board members accused him of withholding information.

“It’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen and the company he has built,” Altman said, adding that he sees Huang as a hero, and that “heroes have flaws.”

OpenAI and Nvidia have had a close relationship for the last decade, one that has evolved from a simple chip supplier-customer relationship into a potentially circular financing arrangement, in which Nvidia’s money helps fund purchases of its own chips. Most recently, Nvidia agreed to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion backing OpenAI’s Ohio data center project. That’s just one of many such circular deals Nvidia has made to bankroll the AI boom while fueling demand for its own chips.

Altman said he’s not worried that the Bank of Nvidia will dry up.

“Nvidia is, like, a behemoth of a company,” he said. “I think people still trust their guarantees very much.”

Altman acknowledged the “ambition” Huang brought to the industry, the scale of which “has been quite important.” But he didn’t go so far as to agree with the many who worry about ripple effects from Huang’s departure.

“I think there’s so much demand, and it’s so clear that AI is real, and people want to use it, and the revenues and demand are growing so strongly that I think the industry will be fine,” Altman said. “But again, I think Jensen has played this extremely special and valuable role as someone to really drive things forward with great ambition.”

items.title: Italian regulator fines Meta $886 million for violating data privacy law
items.summary: The crackdown on Meta’s Facebook platform involved the company’s alleged use of its “camera roll” suggestions option, launched in 2023, to browse Android users’ photo galleries to recommend posts they could enhance with personal photos and videos.
items.content:
Image: Kelly Sikkema via Unsplash Italian regulator fines Meta $886 million for violating data privacy law

Italy’s data protection regulator announced a €805 million ($886 million) fine against Meta on Saturday, saying the social media giant accessed user photos and videos without their specific consent or properly informing them.

The fine, announced Saturday, is one of the biggest the Italian regulator — known as the Garante — has ever issued.

The crackdown on Meta’s Facebook platform involved the company’s alleged use of its “camera roll” suggestions option, launched in 2023, to browse Android users’ photo galleries to recommend posts they could enhance with personal photos and videos. In addition to the photos and videos, the regulator said, Facebook accessed related metadata.

The investigation found Meta asked users to access their camera roll through a single permission that “applies across the entire app covering multiple features with different requirements,” according to a Garante press release .

The permission is preceded by a “non-specific notice” to enable other features, the press release said, failing to make clear to users that they are consenting to suggestions from the camera roll, the regulator said. It also alleged the feature was turned on by default.

“When given in full, such permission allows the app to access the entire photo library on the device, usually on a permanent basis, without the user or [regulators] being able to verify what information is actually being used,” the press release said.

The practice violates Italian data protection regulations safeguarding “the smartphone as part of the individual’s private sphere,” according to a Garate press release.

“Consequently, any access to the information stored on such devices requires free and informed consent, regardless of whether data is transmitted or any harm occurs,” the press release said.

Meta had argued the Garante lacked jurisdiction to issue the fine, but the regulator dismissed that claim.

A Meta spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but told other news outlets in a statement that the company strongly disagrees with the decision and plans to appeal what it called the “disproportionate” fine amount.

The tech giant has been under fire worldwide in recent months, losing multiple court cases in the U.S., including an October decision in which the company was fined $25 billion for deceiving consumers about how it uses their data.

In addition to the fine, the Garante has ordered Meta to make several changes in the next 60 days, including by obtaining consent through a request that is “separate and specific to the feature” and clearly explaining what it is used for. Meta also must begin disabling the option by default.

The unusually high fine is due to the fact that about 20 million Italian Android users were impacted, the long time period over which the violation occurred and the company’s lack of cooperation during the probe, the press release said.

Earlier in her career Suzanne covered the Boston Police Department for the Boston Globe and two presidential campaign cycles for Newsweek. She lives in Washington with her husband and three children.

items.title: King Charles opens new HQ for National Cyber Force, UK’s offensive hacking unit
items.summary: A building near the Lancashire village of Samlesbury in northwest England is officially the headquarters for the secretive unit that runs the Britain's offensive cyber operations.
items.content:
GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler shows King Charles III around the new HQ for the National Cyber Force on November 16, 2026. Image: NCF King Charles opens new HQ for National Cyber Force, UK’s offensive hacking unit

King Charles III on Monday opened the new headquarters of Britain’s National Cyber Force, the secretive unit that runs the country’s offensive cyber operations against hostile states, terrorists and criminals.

Staff are already working in the building near the Lancashire village of Samlesbury in northwest England, named Ribble House after the nearby river and Ribble Valley. The government chose the village as the force’s permanent home five years ago and committed £5 billion ($6.5 billion) to the NCF through 2030.

The NCF brings together staff from the cyber and signals intelligence agency GCHQ, the Ministry of Defence, the Secret Intelligence Service (MI6) and the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory. Officials say it carries out operations every day.

“In an age of radical uncertainty, contested geopolitics, and rapidly changing technology, the NCF keeps the country safe by delivering high-impact cyber operations every single day against those who threaten our interests,” said GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler who showed the king around the site.

As first reported by Recorded Future News, a new commander is currently in charge at the NCF, replacing Air Vice-Marshal Tim Neal-Hopes in September, although officials have yet to name them publicly. Neal-Hopes took over in October 2023 from James Babbage, a former GCHQ officer who subsequently moved to the National Crime Agency.

To date, the NCF has rarely discussed its work in public, saying disclosures would undermine the effects of its covert operations. In a 2023 doctrine paper , it described its operations as “accountable, precise, and calibrated,” in a way that was fundamentally different from those practiced by Britain’s adversaries.

Gen. Sir Rob Magowan, commander of Cyber and Specialist Operations Command, said: “The opening of the National Cyber Force’s new headquarters marks a significant milestone in strengthening the UK’s ability to combat threats in an increasingly contested world.

“We must be ready to confront, deter and prevail in the cyber domain, taking the initiative against those who threaten our national security. The National Cyber Force plays a vital role in giving the UK that advantage,” he added.

British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called the headquarters “a major investment in the North West, in defence innovation, and in keeping our country safe.”

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: “As hostile actors use cyberattacks to disrupt our way of life and cause us harm, our world class intelligence agencies ensure that we can tackle those threats head-on.”

Ribble House’s ceremonial opening comes on the same day a House of Lords committee warned the country is “underprepared” for “potentially catastrophic risks” including cyberattacks from Russia, China and Iran.

The committee said the government “appears complacent” and stressed the “need to move fast to turn things around.”

items.title: Russia denies intercepting Romanian government emails
items.summary: Russia has denied accusations that its state-backed hackers targeted a Romanian government institution in an attempt to intercept emails exchanged with NATO and the European Union.
items.content:
Image: Petru-Rareș Panaite / Unsplash Russia denies intercepting Romanian government emails

Russia has denied accusations that its state-backed hackers targeted a Romanian government institution in an attempt to intercept emails exchanged with NATO and the European Union.

The Russian Embassy in Bucharest on Monday dismissed the allegations as fabricated, accusing Romanian intelligence services of spreading false claims about Moscow's involvement in cyberattacks.

"This is yet another fabrication by the Romanian intelligence services, part of their ongoing narrative about Russia's mythical 'hybrid attacks,'" the embassy said in a statement published on Telegram in response to questions from Reuters.

The embassy accused Romanian authorities of trying to discredit Russia and said Bucharest had provided no concrete evidence to support its claims.

The denial comes days after Romania's domestic intelligence agency (SRI) said it had detected and stopped a cyberattack attributed to Turla, a long-running Russian espionage group linked to Moscow's Federal Security Service (FSB).

According to the agency, the hackers infiltrated the systems of an unidentified government institution in December 2025 by exploiting vulnerabilities in Microsoft software.

Romanian cybersecurity specialists contained the intrusion and restored the affected email service, the agency said, adding that investigators had found no evidence that sensitive information had been stolen.

The disclosure followed research published earlier this month by Slovak cybersecurity firm ESET, which uncovered a previously unknown hacking toolkit used by Turla to compromise government email servers in Romania and Kazakhstan.

According to ESET, the malware deployed against the Romanian target was specifically configured to collect emails exchanged with NATO and EU institutions.

Romania's intelligence agency said it was also investigating other potentially related cyber operations linked to Russia.

Moscow has for years denied accusations of carrying out cyberattacks and other hostile operations against Western countries.

items.title: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
items.summary: Microsoft says a software bug introduced in July caused last week's worldwide Microsoft 365 outage, triggering a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive. [...]
items.content:
Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage

Microsoft says a software bug introduced in July caused last week's worldwide Microsoft 365 outage, triggering a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive.

The nearly 24-hour outage on November 12 disrupted Microsoft 365 services worldwide , including Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, and Copilot, leaving users unable to access their email and causing significant delays in message delivery.

In a preliminary post-incident report shared in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, the company said the outage was caused by three problems: a previously undetected software bug, increased traffic after a Microsoft Teams failover, and reduced server capacity.

The incident began at 11:20 AM ET on Thursday, November 12, and continued until 11:10 AM ET the following day, when Microsoft confirmed that services were full restored.

According to Microsoft, the software bug was introduced in July through an update developed for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.

While the update had been deployed for more than three months without issues, it contained a bug that could overwhelm servers under certain traffic conditions, causing them to stop responding.

Microsoft says its tests of the update did not detect the bug as it used less powerful testing hardware than the production servers.

"Our normal load testing did not detect the latent issue because the traffic mix and SKUs used in our labs," Microsoft explained in its preliminary report.

"The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores."

The bug was eventually triggered after Microsoft Teams automatically switched to the networking infrastructure used by Exchange Online approximately 15 hours before the outage, increasing traffic on those servers.

Microsoft Teams also experienced a separate outage earlier that day, but it is unclear whether the two incidents are related.

To make matters worse, Microsoft says nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was already offline due to an unrelated issue. While the infrastructure had sufficient capacity to handle the reduction, the combination of increased traffic and reduced capacity triggered the software bug.

As servers stopped responding, Microsoft's systems redirected users to other available servers, which also became overwhelmed by the additional traffic and failed as well.

"In less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive," explained Microsoft.

Microsoft says safeguards designed to prevent problems from spreading between regions also failed to contain the cascading outages, allowing the disruption to spread worldwide.

While other Microsoft 365 services, like Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint, could switch to alternative infrastructure and recover earlier, Exchange Online could not make the same switch, leaving users unable to access their mailboxes.

Microsoft says recovery was difficult because restarting affected servers caused them to be quickly overwhelmed again by backed-up traffic.

After identifying the bug, Microsoft engineers developed a fix and deployed it across affected servers, allowing services to stabilize throughout Friday.

Microsoft confirmed that active customer impact had ended by 11:10 AM ET on November 13.

The company says it has since increased capacity, improved monitoring, and added safeguards to prevent traffic redirection from triggering similar cascading failures.

In a separate statement on X, Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, apologized for the disruption.

items.content:
강원대학교 산학협력단이 외부 해킹으로 개인정보가 유출된 데 이어 연구통합관리시스템 접속 중단에 따른 연구비 집행 차질 가능성까지 공식 안내했다. 개인정보 유출 사고가 대학 연구행정 업무에 영향을 미칠 수 있는 상황으로 확대되면서 시스템 복구와 연구비 집행 정상화 여부에 관심이 쏠리고 있다.

강원대학교 산학협력단은 11월 16일 오후 2시 16분 공식 홈페이지에 ‘[긴급] 연구통합관리시스템 접속 중단 안내’를 게시하고, 외부 해킹 사고에 따른 긴급 점검으로 연구통합관리시스템 이용과 연구비 집행업무에 일부 차질이 발생할 수 있다고 밝혔다.

대학 측은 현재 사고에 따른 시스템 운영 상황을 점검하고 있으며, 연구비 집행을 위한 대체방안과 향후 조치사항을 확인되는 대로 안내하겠다는 입장이다.

이번 공지는 앞서 발생한 개인정보 유출 사고의 후속 조치다. 강원대학교 산학협력단은 지난 15일 연구통합관리시스템에서 개인정보 유출이 발생한 사실을 공개했다. 대학 측에 따르면 사고는 11월 14일 오전 6시 22분경 발생했으며, 외부 비인가자가 시스템에 접근해 사용자 개인정보를 탈취한 것으로 확인됐다.

유출 정보에는 연구통합관리시스템 이용자의 개인정보가 포함됐으며, 생년월일 정보가 포함된 사례도 27건 확인됐다. 다만 전체 개인정보 유출 규모와 실제 피해 인원은 명확하게 공개되지 않았다.

연구통합관리시스템은 대학 산학협력단이 연구과제와 연구비 집행 등 연구행정 업무를 처리하는 데 사용하는 주요 시스템이다. 이 시스템의 접속이 중단되면 연구비 신청과 지급, 집행내역 처리, 정산 등 관련 업무에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

특히 연구과제를 수행하는 교수와 연구원, 산학협력단 실무자들은 연구비 집행 일정에 따라 각종 비용을 처리해야 하는 만큼 시스템 중단이 장기화할 경우 업무상 불편이 커질 가능성이 있다.

이번 사고가 개인정보 유출에 그치지 않고 대학의 연구행정 업무 연속성 문제로 연결될 수 있다는 점에서 복구 일정과 대체 업무처리 체계 마련 여부가 중요해졌다.

현재 여러 대학의 연구행정시스템에서 비슷한 시기에 침해사고 또는 보안상 이상 징후가 확인되면서 외부 유지보수 환경이나 공통 시스템을 통한 공격 가능성을 면밀히 조사할 필요가 있다.
